title: Users & teams
description: Who can sign in, their roles and teams. Roles give default rights everywhere; access lists on processes and platforms can narrow them down.
resetConfirm: Reset the password of {{user}}? Their sessions are signed out.

temp.title: Temporary password
temp.text: Give this password to {{user}} through a secure channel. It is shown only once; the user has to choose a new password at the first sign-in.

teams.title: Teams
teams.none: No teams yet. Teams group users so that access lists and task assignments can refer to them (e.g. team:service desk).
teams.deleteConfirm: Delete team "{{name}}"? Access entries that name it stop matching anyone.

roles.title: Roles
roles.hint: Roles are defaults. A process or platform with an access list only grants the rights listed there (plus administrators and, for processes, the owner). Approval steps can additionally be assigned to specific users, teams or roles and require a second person (four-eyes principle).

userModal.ssoHint: Single sign-on users are created automatically at their first sign-in (if the provider allows it). You can also create them here in advance with exactly their SSO user name (e.g. the e-mail / UPN) to assign roles – the account is linked at the first sign-in.
userModal.initialPasswordHint: Leave empty to generate a temporary password. The user must change it at the first sign-in either way.
userModal.adminWarning: Administrators can manage users, platforms and credentials and see everything.
userModal.noPasswordHint: Password sign-in is turned off: the account gets no password. It is linked at its first single sign-on with exactly this user name (e.g. the e-mail / UPN).
userModal.signInHint: A single sign-on account has no password. Only this provider can claim it at the first sign-in, with exactly this user name.
userModal.signInBindHint: Choosing a provider removes the password and signs the account out; only that provider can then claim it, with exactly this user name.
userModal.managedHint: Greyed-out fields come from the single sign-on provider at every sign-in.

sso.removeConfirm: Remove single sign-on "{{name}}"? Users of this provider can no longer sign in (their accounts and history stay).
sso.title: Single sign-on
sso.redirectHint: Register this as redirect URI (type Web) in your identity provider / Entra app registration:
sso.redirectMatch: It must match exactly how users open {{brand}} (host name and http/https). Entra ID only accepts http for localhost.
sso.none: No single sign-on configured. Add Microsoft Entra ID or any OpenID Connect provider (Okta, Keycloak, Google Workspace, ADFS …).

provider.tenantHint: From the app registration overview in Entra ID
provider.issuerEntraHint: Computed from the tenant ID; edit only for special clouds
provider.issuerHint: The OpenID Connect issuer; /.well-known/openid-configuration must be reachable below it
provider.secretHint: Stored encrypted with the master passphrase
provider.entraHint: In the Entra app registration define App roles (e.g. SM.Operators), assign users/groups to them in Enterprise applications, and map the role values here (claim roles). Alternatively emit the groups claim and map group object IDs (max. 200 groups per token).
provider.noMappings: No mappings – users only get the default roles below.
provider.defaultRolesHint: Every user signing in with this provider gets these roles (in addition to mapped ones)
provider.autoProvisionHint: Otherwise an administrator has to create the user first (same user name); it is linked on the first sign-in.
provider.syncRoles: Sync roles and mapped teams at every sign-in
provider.syncRolesHint: Roles come from the identity provider; changes made here are overwritten at the next sign-in.
provider.requireMapping: Deny sign-in when no mapping matches
provider.presetHint: Pre-fills the settings below. Every value stays editable.

presetHints.entra: App roles in the app registration become the roles claim. Entra ID sends email_verified only as an optional claim, so the user name comes from preferred_username (the UPN) and people are identified by tenant + object id (tid, oid).
presetHints.keycloak: Add a “Group Membership” mapper (claim groups, without full path) to the client so groups reach the token. Keycloak sends email_verified.
presetHints.okta: Add a groups claim to the authorization server (or the app) and the scope groups. Okta sends email_verified.
presetHints.google: Google sends no groups and no preferred_username: the verified e-mail address names the account. Enter your Workspace domain as required value of the claim hd – otherwise any Google account may sign in.
presetHints.authentik: The issuer ends with the application slug and a slash. Authentik sends groups with the default “profile” scope mapping.
presetHints.generic: Any OpenID Connect provider: issuer, client and the claim names your provider uses.

provider.displayNameTemplateHint: Claims in braces, e.g. {given_name} {family_name}. Empty: the display name claim.
provider.emailVerifiedByProviderHint: Only for providers that never send email_verified. Then the e-mail claim may name or identify accounts without it – make sure the provider really verifies every address.
provider.useUserinfoHint: For claims the ID token leaves out. Where both have a claim, the ID token wins.
provider.stableId: Claims that identify a person for good
provider.stableIdHint: Together with the issuer. Use claims nobody can change (sub; Entra ID: tid and oid). After a change, each account is re-linked at its next sign-in through its issuer + sub.
provider.stableIdRequired: Enter at least one claim (usually sub)
provider.accountsSection: Accounts: linking, required claims, names and profile fields
provider.linkExisting: Existing accounts at the first sign-in
provider.linkExistingHint: What happens when someone signs in for the first time and an account with their user name exists already. A local administrator account is never linked by its name.

linkPolicies.bound: Only accounts an administrator bound to this provider
linkPolicies.byName: Any local account with the same user name

linkPolicyHints.bound: Recommended. Bind an account under Users & teams → Edit user → Signs in with.
linkPolicyHints.byName: Whoever has this user name at the provider gets the local account, its roles and its history.
linkPolicyHints.never: Existing accounts – also bound ones – are not linked; a new identity with a taken user name is refused.

provider.requiredClaimsHint: Sign-in only when the claim has one of the values, e.g. hd = your Google Workspace domain, tid = your Entra tenant id.

syncRules.create: Only when the account is created or linked

provider.profileFieldsHint: Read-only fields on the account, shown on the user page and in the public API (users). Nested claims with dots, e.g. address.locality.
provider.keepLinks: Keep the existing accounts linked to the new issuer
provider.keepLinksHint: Only when the new issuer issues the same subjects (e.g. a renamed host). Otherwise the links stay with the former issuer and those people get no access through the new one.

warnings.title: Check these settings
warnings.LINK_BY_NAME: Existing local accounts are linked by their user name: whoever has that name at the provider gets the account. Prefer “Only accounts an administrator bound to this provider”.
warnings.MULTI_TENANT_ISSUER: Accounts of any organisation can sign in with this issuer. Add a required claim tid with your tenant id.
warnings.TENANT_INFLUENCED_CLAIM: The claim {{claim}} is set by each organisation’s administrators – with a multi-tenant issuer another organisation can send any value. Use claims your organisation controls (nOAuth).
warnings.USER_INFLUENCED_CLAIM: People can often change the claim {{claim}} themselves – do not name or identify accounts by it.
warnings.MUTABLE_STABLE_ID: The stable identifier uses claims that can change ({{claims}}): when they change, the person loses the account, and someone else may get it. Use sub (Entra ID: tid and oid).
warnings.STRIP_DOMAIN: Without the domain, people of different domains get the same user name (max@a.com and max@b.com → max): the second one is refused.
warnings.NO_DOMAIN_RESTRICTION: Any Google account can sign in. Add the required claim hd with your Workspace domain.
warnings.EMAIL_TRUSTED: E-mail addresses are trusted without email_verified. Only when the provider verifies every address.
warnings.USERNAME_COLLISIONS: Accounts of this provider that get the same user name under this rule: {{names}}.

test.title: Test sign-in
test.hint: Sign in once through this provider in a new window: you see the claims it sends and what a sign-in would do with the settings in this form. Nothing signs in, no account is created, linked or changed.
test.saveFirst: Save the provider first, then test the sign-in.
test.notStarted: The test sign-in could not start
test.waiting: Waiting for the sign-in in the other window …
test.previewHint: With the settings in this form – unsaved changes included.

relinkFrom.legacy: Found by its link from an earlier version (provider + sub); the link is renewed with the stable identifier.
relinkFrom.sub: Found by its earlier issuer + sub; the link is renewed with the stable identifier.

notes.USERNAME_FALLBACK: The claim {{claim}} was not sent – the user name comes from {{from}}.
notes.GROUPS_OVERAGE: The token left the groups out (too many groups; claim {{claim}}). No roles come from them. Assign groups to the application, use app roles or a group filter.
notes.USERINFO_USED: Claims from the userinfo endpoint are used too.

profileValues.title: From the sign-in provider
profileValues.hint: Read-only: updated by the single sign-on provider.
